cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He's just told them they're God's children and co-heirs with Christ, if they suffer with Him so they'll be glorified with Him (Romans 8:16-17). Now he sets the suffering and the glory side by side.

cards.question: Paul weighs our present sufferings against the glory that will be revealed in us. What does he conclude?

answers.text: The sufferings are not comparable to the glory
The sufferings are about equal to the glory
The sufferings will last longer than the glory

cards.text: Then Paul zooms out past people. The creation itself is waiting, and not bored waiting, EAGER waiting, like me pressed up against the oven window for the last two minutes of a batch.

cards.question: Paul says the creation waits in eager expectation for a revelation. Whose revelation is it?

cards.text: Paul says the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will. Friend, I KNOW futility, because I spent years in the back of a junk drawer and not ONE cookie came out of it.

cards.question: Paul says the creation was subjected to futility because of the One who subjected it.
Paul says the creation was subjected to futility in hope. What does that hope say will happen to the creation itself?

answers.text: It will be set free from its decay
It will be returned to the garden
It will be at rest from all storms

cards.text: Then Paul says the whole creation has been groaning together until now, and he's not talking about the groan you make when your alarm goes off. He's got a very specific kind of pain in mind.

cards.question: Paul says the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of ___ until the present time.

cards.text: Not only that. Paul says we who have the firstfruits of the Spirit groan inwardly too, like I do when a whole tray sticks to the pan and I smile like it's FINE.

cards.question: While believers groan inwardly, Paul says they wait eagerly for their adoption as sons. What does Paul say that adoption is?

answers.text: A rest from all their labor
A home in the promised land

cards.text: Paul says in this hope we were saved. Then he asks what it means to hope for something you can already see.

cards.question: Paul says hope that is seen is still real hope.
If we hope for what we do not yet see, Paul says we wait for it ___.

cards.text: In the same way, Paul says, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. He names one in particular, and no, friend, it's NOT my weakness for warm chocolate chips.

cards.question: Paul says we always know how we ought to pray.

cards.text: Ever start a prayer and get stuck right after "Lord…"? Me too, friend, and Paul says the Spirit Himself intercedes for us.

cards.question: Paul says the Spirit intercedes for us with groans too deep for ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, and he tells us why.

cards.question: Paul says the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.

cards.text: Then comes a line a lot of believers know by heart: we know that God works all things together for good. ALL things, friend, not just the batches that come out pretty.

cards.question: Paul says God works all things together for the good of those who love Him.

cards.text: Those who love Him are also called according to His purpose, Paul says. Then he backs up even further, and I mean WAY back: those God foreknew, He also predestined.

cards.question: Paul says those God foreknew, He predestined for something. What is it?

answers.text: To be conformed to the image of His Son
To be made servants in His Son's kingdom
To be set as priests in His holy temple

cards.question: Paul says God's Son would be the ___ among many brothers.

cards.text: Then Paul links it all together like a chain: those He predestined, He also called, and those He called, He also justified.

cards.question: Paul's chain keeps going past those God justified. Where does it end?
